subject.title: feat(channels): core-owned durable ingress drain — one turn-adoption lifecycle for Telegram and WhatsApp

question: Should the durable ingress drain and turn-adoption lifecycle become a permanent public plugin SDK contract in this PR, and if so which claim/retry helpers are intentionally supported for external plugins?
rationale: The generic core ownership is plausible and consistent with the architecture, but the branch adds a substantial compatibility-sensitive SDK surface immediately after a major SDK contraction; code review cannot decide which internals maintainers intend to support long term.

options.title: Approve a narrower public seam
options.body: Keep the core drain and lifecycle factory public, retain claim/retry implementation helpers inside core, and require live Telegram and WhatsApp proof before merge.

options.title: Approve the current SDK surface
options.body: Intentionally support the complete exported drain, claim-owner, retry, and compatibility-mirror surface as a permanent external plugin contract.

options.title: Keep the drain bundled-only first
options.body: Land or restack the Telegram and WhatsApp migration using internal bundled-plugin wiring, then design a public SDK after another channel demonstrates external demand.

recommendation.title: Approve a narrower public seam
recommendation.body: Keep the core drain and lifecycle factory public, retain claim/retry implementation helpers inside core, and require live Telegram and WhatsApp proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision primarily concerns the permanent plugin SDK contract and follows their recent SDK surface-narrowing work.
